root_causes: Inefficient action selection: the agent repeatedly executed Wait and Explore[bedroom_1] without progressing object manipulation, leading to unnecessary steps and negative reward accumulation.

Lack of task decomposition into concrete subtasks (navigate → find object → pick → navigate → place), causing the planner to remain at planning step 1 with no visible transition to object interaction.
Insufficient use of task state feedback: despite Completed propositions staying at 0/5 for many steps, the agent did not adapt its strategy or switch to targeted search/manipulation behaviors.

Exploration policy not terminating or refining: Explore[bedroom_1] was invoked many times from the same pose and orientation (-7.11, -2.07, facing north), indicating no effective spatial exploration or view change.
improvement_suggestions: Introduce a higher-level task manager that explicitly sequences subtasks for each object (e.g., for toy_fire_truck_0: locate → navigate → pick → navigate to chest_of_drawers_X → place) and monitors progress on each proposition.
Implement an exploration controller that enforces pose and viewpoint diversity (move and rotate) rather than repeatedly exploring from the same position and orientation.

Leverage task progress signals (Completed propositions) to trigger strategy revision: if propositions remain at 0 for N steps, switch from generic Explore to targeted object search or navigation to likely receptacles.
Add termination/guard conditions for low-information actions like Wait and generic Explore to avoid long loops when no new observations or state changes are produced.
Incorporate memory of visited locations and views in the bedroom so Explore will prioritize unvisited regions and known locations of relevant objects and receptacles.

Tighten reward shaping so that prolonged non-progress (repeated Wait/Explore with no new propositions completed) is penalized more strongly, encouraging the planner to attempt manipulation actions earlier.
overall_assessment: The episode is marked as a success but the trajectory is highly inefficient, spending many steps on repetitive Wait and Explore actions without observable progress on the specified object placements. Execution achieved the goal but with poor use of time and actions.
task_instruction: relocate the toy fire truck to the chest of drawers. place the toy food items in a new chest of drawers. Place the stuffed toy on the bed.
